column1: repute§The firm's repute rests on four decades of quiet work and one very public failure in 1994.§这家公司的**声誉**建立在四十年默默无闻的工作和 1994 年一次极其公开的失败之上。§re（再）+ put（思量，同 compute 计算）→ 大家反复评估出的名声
pant§He arrived panting after four flights of stairs and delivered the news in nine broken words.§他爬完四层楼**气喘吁吁**地赶到，用九个断断续续的词说出了消息。§
quench§Nothing quenched the fire in the hold until the crew deliberately flooded four adjacent compartments.§直到船员刻意向相邻的四个舱室注水，货舱里的火才被**扑灭**。§
implement§They implemented four of the nine recommendations and reported, in the annual review, full compliance.§他们**执行**了九条建议中的四条，却在年度报告里宣称完全落实。§im（进入）+ ple（填满，同 complete 完整的）→ 把方案填实
encapsulated§The whole argument is encapsulated in one sentence on page four, and the other ninety pages restate it.§整个论点被**浓缩**在第四页的一句话里，其余九十页都在重述它。§en（进入）+ capsul（小盒，同 capsule 胶囊）
contaminate§One faulty valve contaminated four batches, and the recall reached nine countries within a week.§一个故障阀门**污染**了四个批次，召回一周内波及九个国家。§con（一起）+ tamin ← tag（接触，同 contact 接触）
wind ensemble§The wind ensemble has nine players and performs music written, originally, for four times that many.§这个**管乐团**有九名乐手，演奏的却是原本为四倍人数所写的音乐。§
cinematography§The cinematography is the film's real achievement: four camera positions and no artificial light at all.§**电影摄影**才是这部片子真正的成就——四个机位，完全不用人工光。§kinema（运动）+ graph（记录，同 graphic 图形的）
tenant§The tenant had lived there nine years and learned about the sale from a notice on the door.§这位**租客**已住九年，却是从门上一张告示得知房子要卖。§ten（拿住，同 contain 容纳）→ 持有使用权的人
symposium§The symposium ran four days and produced one genuinely new idea, which came up over dinner.§这场**研讨会**开了四天，产生了一个真正的新想法，而它是在晚餐时冒出来的。§syn（一起）+ pos（喝）→ 古希腊的饮宴清谈
preoccupation§His preoccupation with cost blinded him to a risk that four colleagues had raised in writing.§他对成本的**执念**让他看不见一项四位同事曾书面提出的风险。§pre（在前）+ occupy（占据）→ 心思被先占住
refraction§Refraction makes the pole look bent, and four centuries of fishermen learned to aim below the fish.§**折射**让杆子看着是弯的，四个世纪的渔民学会了瞄准鱼的下方。§re（回）+ fract（折断，同 fracture 骨折）
conciliate§She conciliated two departments that had not exchanged a civil word in nine years.§她**调和**了两个九年没说过一句客气话的部门。§con（一起）+ cili ← cal（召唤，同 council 议会）
informed§One informed guess from the caretaker was worth more than four weeks of formal investigation.§看管人一个**内行的**猜测，抵得上四周的正式调查还不止。§
contempt§His contempt for the process was obvious, and he followed every step of it exactly.§他对这套流程的**轻蔑**显而易见，却一步不差地照做了。§con（加强）+ temn（轻视）
courageous§The courageous decision was the boring one: say nothing publicly and fix it over nine months.§**勇敢的**决定其实是那个乏味的——公开不作声，用九个月把它修好。§cour（心）
lash§The crew lashed four barrels to the deck, and only those four survived the night.§船员把四只桶**捆绑**在甲板上，而只有那四只熬过了那一夜。§
staggering§The staggering figure is on page nine: four hundred thousand hours of unpaid overtime a year.§那个**惊人的**数字在第九页——每年四十万小时无偿加班。§
breed§The breed was down to nine animals in 1974 and numbers about four thousand today.§这个**品种**在 1974 年只剩九只，如今约有四千只。§
tributary§The tributary carries a third of the water and, in four of the last nine years, most of the pollution.§这条**支流**输送三分之一的水量，而在过去九年中的四年里输送了大部分污染物。§tribut（缴纳，同 contribute 贡献）→ 向主流「进贡」
obligate§The statute obligates four agencies to publish and gives none of them a deadline for doing so.§这部法律**强制**四家机构公布，却没给其中任何一家规定期限。§ob（向）+ lig（捆绑，同 ligament 韧带）
slacken§The pace slackened after the fourth hour, and the error rate fell by about nine percent.§第四小时后节奏**放缓**，错误率下降了约百分之九。§slack（松弛）
saddle§The reorganization saddled four managers with work that nine people had previously shared between them.§这次重组让四位经理**扛下**了此前九个人分担的工作。§
agonize§She agonized for nine weeks over a decision that, once made, took four days to implement.§她为一个做出后四天就能执行的决定**苦苦煎熬**了九周。§
bluff§He bluffed for four minutes, and the other side folded without ever asking to see the figures.§他**虚张声势**了四分钟，对方没要求看数字就让步了。§

emancipate§The reform emancipated four million people on paper and reached, in practice, about nine hundred thousand.§这项改革在纸面上**解放**了四百万人，实际惠及约九十万。§e（出）+ man（手，同 manual 手工的）+ cap（拿，同 capture 捕获）→ 脱离掌控
vulgar§The joke was vulgar and, in the four seconds it took, told the room exactly who he was.§这个玩笑**粗俗**，而在它持续的四秒里，让全场看清了他是什么人。§vulg（大众，同 divulge 泄露）→ 街头的
warp§Nine months of damp warped four of the doors, and none of them has closed properly since.§九个月的潮湿**扭曲**了四扇门，此后没有一扇能关严。§
gallop§Costs galloped from four hundred thousand to nine million while the design was still being argued about.§设计还在争论时，成本就从四十万**飞涨**到九百万。§
shift§The shift in opinion took about four years and is visible, in the surveys, from 1994 onward.§这次观点的**转变**用了约四年，从 1994 年起在调查中就看得出来。§
plunge§Attendance plunged from nine hundred to forty in four weeks, and nobody asked the visitors why.§参观人数四周内从九百**骤降**到四十，而没人问过访客原因。§
insuperable§The obstacle looked insuperable for nine years and turned out to be a single missing signature.§这道障碍**看似无法逾越**了九年，结果只是一个缺失的签名。§in（不）+ super（在上）→ 翻不过去
warrant§Nothing in the file warrants a nine-month delay, and the department has not tried to explain one.§卷宗里没有任何东西能**证明**九个月的延误是正当的，而部门也没试图解释。§
interject§She interjected four words that changed the direction of a discussion nine people had lost control of.§她插了四个词，**打断**并改变了一场九个人已失控的讨论的方向。§inter（在中间）+ ject（投掷，同 project 投射）
enduring§The most enduring part of the reform is the one nobody argued about: a four-line reporting rule.§这项改革最**持久的**部分是无人争议的那条——四行的报告规定。§en（进入）+ dur（坚硬，同 durable 耐久的）
ineluctable§The conclusion is ineluctable once the fourth assumption is granted, and the fourth is the weak one.§一旦承认第四个假设，结论就**无可逃避**，而第四个恰恰是薄弱的那个。§in（不）+ e（出）+ luct（挣扎，同 reluctant 勉强的）→ 挣不脱
rigid§The rules are rigid where flexibility would cost nothing and vague where precision would matter.§这些规则在灵活不会有代价的地方**僵硬**，在精确才要紧的地方含糊。§rig（僵硬，同 rigor 严格）
grudgingly§He grudgingly conceded four points and, nine years later, cited each of them as his own.§他**不情愿地**让了四步，九年后又把每一步都说成自己的主张。§grudge（怨恨）
inadvertently§She inadvertently deleted nine months of records and rebuilt four of them from printed copies.§她**无意中**删掉了九个月的记录，又从纸质副本重建了其中四个月。§in（不）+ ad（向）+ vert（转，同 convert 转变）→ 心思没转过去
perturbation§A small perturbation in the orbit revealed a body that four surveys had failed to detect.§轨道上一个小小的**扰动**揭示出一个四次巡天都没探测到的天体。§per（彻底）+ turb（搅动，同 turbulence 湍流）
predicate§The whole argument is predicated on a figure that turned out, four years later, to be wrong.§整个论证**建立在**一个四年后被证明是错的数字上。§pre（在前）+ dic（说，同 dictate 口述）
apostle§He became the apostle of a method that four laboratories had abandoned as unworkable.§他成了一种被四家实验室弃为不可行的方法的**倡导者**。§apo（离开）+ stol（派遣）→ 被派出去传话的人
defect§The defect appeared in about one unit in nine and only after four hundred hours of use.§这个**缺陷**约每九台出现一次，且只在使用四百小时后出现。§de（离开）+ fect（做，同 perfect 完美的）
detriment§The delay was to the detriment of nine hundred families and to the advantage of exactly one company.§这次延误**损害**了九百个家庭，只对一家公司有利。§de（离开）+ trit（磨损，同 attrition 消耗）
exasperate§Four rounds of the same question exasperated a witness who had answered it identically each time.§同一个问题问了四轮，**激怒**了一位每次都给出相同答案的证人。§ex（加强）+ asper（粗糙，同 asperity 严酷）
testament§The building is a testament to nine years of stubbornness and about four hundred small compromises.§这栋建筑是九年固执与约四百次小妥协的**明证**。§test（作证，同 testify 作证）
woeful§The woeful state of the records was known in 1994 and remained unaddressed for the next nine years.§记录的**糟糕**状况 1994 年就已知晓，此后九年无人处理。§woe（悲哀）
extricate§It took four lawyers and nine months to extricate the company from a contract it had signed in a day.§四位律师、九个月，才把公司从一份一天就签下的合同里**解脱**出来。§ex（出）+ tric（麻烦，同 intricate 复杂的）→ 从缠结中拉出来
impertinent§The impertinent question was the only one that produced a straight answer in four hours.§这个**唐突无礼的**问题，是四小时里唯一换来直接答复的。§im（不）+ pertinent（相关的）
dissemble§He dissembled for nine minutes and then, asked the same thing a fourth time, simply told the truth.§他**掩饰**了九分钟，第四次被问到同一件事时干脆说了实话。§dis（否定）+ semble（相似，同 resemble 相似）
admonish§The judge admonished both counsel and, in the ruling itself, agreed with neither of them.§法官**告诫**了双方律师，而在裁定中两边都不支持。§ad（向）+ mon（提醒，同 monitor 监视器）
inveterate§An inveterate note-taker, he left nine thousand cards that four researchers are still working through.§他是个**积习难改的**记笔记者，留下九千张卡片，四位研究者至今仍在整理。§in（在内）+ veter（年老，同 veteran 老兵）→ 老毛病
chagrin§Much to her chagrin, the idea she had proposed four years earlier was adopted under someone else's name.§令她**懊恼**的是，她四年前提出的想法以别人的名义被采纳了。§
clemency§The board showed clemency in nine cases that year and, in the four that mattered publicly, none at all.§那年董事会在九起案件中显示了**宽厚**，而在四起备受关注的案件中毫无宽容。§clemen（温和）
adulate§Journalists adulated him for four years and, after the accounts were published, could not be found.§记者**吹捧**了他四年，账目公布后就找不到人了。§
elucidate§One diagram elucidated a mechanism that nine hundred words of text had failed to convey.§一张图**阐明**了九百字文字都没能传达的机制。§e（出）+ lucid（明亮，同 lucid 清晰的）
whim§The route was chosen on a whim in 1908 and has carried four generations of traffic since.§这条路线 1908 年是**一时兴起**定下的，此后承载了四代人的往来。§
foment§Four anonymous letters fomented a dispute that had been quietly settled nine months earlier.§四封匿名信**煽起**了一场九个月前已悄悄平息的争端。§foment（热敷）→ 捂热了让它发作
provided§The council will fund the repair, provided the four owners agree in writing within nine weeks.§议会将资助维修，**前提是**四位业主在九周内书面同意。§
putative§The putative author of the pamphlet died four years before it was printed, which nobody noticed for a century.§这本小册子**被认定的**作者在它印刷前四年就已去世，而这一点一个世纪无人察觉。§put（思量，同 compute 计算）→ 被认为是
inform§Nine years in the wards informs every page of the book, and none of it reads like a lecture.§病房里的九年**渗透**在书的每一页，而没有一页读起来像讲课。§in（进入）+ form（形状）→ 从内部塑造
draw§The exhibition draws four thousand people a week to a town of nine thousand.§这个展览每周**吸引**四千人来到一座九千人的小镇。§
assume§She assumed the post in March and, by September, had reversed four of her predecessor's decisions.§她三月**接任**这个职位，到九月已推翻前任的四个决定。§as（向）+ sum（拿，同 consume 消耗）→ 把担子拿过来
reciprocity§Reciprocity broke down after four years, and neither side has recognized the other's licences since.§**互惠**在四年后破裂，此后双方都不承认对方的执照。§re（回）+ pro（向前）→ 一来一往
understate§The report understates the cost by about nine hundred thousand pounds, which one footnote half admits.§这份报告把成本**低估**了约九十万英镑，一条脚注半承认了这点。§under（不足）+ state（陈述）
register§The change did not register with anyone for four years, and then nine complaints arrived in a week.§这项改动四年没被任何人**察觉**，然后一周内来了九封投诉。§
postulate§The theory postulates four forces, and the fourth has never been observed in ninety years of trying.§这套理论**假定**存在四种力，而第四种在九十年的努力中从未被观测到。§post（在后）+ ul ← pet（要求，同 petition 请愿）→ 先要求承认
stymie§One missing permit stymied a project that four separate agencies had already spent nine months approving.§一份缺失的许可**卡住**了一个四家机构花九个月才批下来的项目。§ 源自高尔夫术语：球挡住了击球线路
laity§The laity outnumbered the clergy nine to one and had, until 1994, no vote at all.§**平信徒**人数是神职人员的九倍，而直到 1994 年都毫无投票权。§lai ← laos（民众）
make a case against§It is easy to make a case against the plan and much harder to name a workable alternative.§**论证反对**这项计划很容易，要说出一个可行的替代方案则难得多。§
make a case for§Nobody could make a case for the fourth option, and the committee adopted it anyway.§没人能为第四个选项**说出支持的理由**，委员会还是采纳了它。§
prone to§The older pumps are prone to failure below four degrees, which explains nine of the eleven incidents.§这些老泵在四度以下**容易**故障，这解释了十一起事故中的九起。§
render§The photograph renders the room larger than it is, and four visitors in ten say so on arrival.§这张照片把房间**呈现**得比实际大，十位访客中有四位一到就这么说。§re（再）+ dere ← dare（给，同 donate 捐赠）→ 交出、呈现
undue§The delay caused undue hardship to nine families, and the ombudsman said so in four paragraphs.§这次延误给九个家庭造成了**不应有的**困难，监察专员用四段这么写了。§un（不）+ due（应有的）
virtually§The line is virtually unused: four passengers a day on a service that costs nine hundred pounds to run.§这条线路**几乎**没人用——每天四名乘客，而运营成本是九百英镑。§virtu（力量／实质，同 virtue 美德）→ 实质上
exonerate§Nine years of records exonerated a man whom four separate inquiries had already condemned.§九年的记录**免除**了一个已被四次独立调查定罪之人的责任。§ex（出）+ oner（重担，同 onerous 繁重的）→ 卸下担子
patronize§He patronizes the staff in a way that four of them have raised formally and nothing has changed.§他对员工**居高临下**，其中四人正式反映过，而什么也没改变。§patr（父亲，同 paternal 父亲的）→ 摆家长架子
commensurate§The salary is not commensurate with the responsibility, which is why the post has been vacant nine months.§薪水与责任**不相称**，这就是这个职位空缺九个月的原因。§com（一起）+ mensur（测量，同 measure 测量）→ 量得上
secularize§The state secularized four hundred monasteries and used the proceeds to fund nine universities.§国家**世俗化**了四百座修道院，用所得资助了九所大学。§secul（世代／尘世）
blithe§His blithe assurance that nothing whatever could go wrong lasted exactly four days and cost nine jobs.§他**满不在乎地**保证绝不会出任何问题，这份保证恰好撑了四天，代价是九个岗位。§
